text:
A: Hi! Can you hear me?
B: Yes. Hello. I'm Tariq.
A: Riya. Nice to meet you. Is this your last one as well?
B: It is. You're the last of the three for me. How have you found it?
A: Yeah, actually fine, everyone's been really nice. Where are you based?
B: Ilford. Gants Hill. And I work in Stratford, so I'm on the Central line most days.
A: Oh my god, no way, I work in Stratford too. And I'm in Leyton. So we've probably been squashed on the same train.
B: Very likely. Eight-fifteen, westbound, standing with someone's backpack in my face.
A: That is literally every morning. What do you do in Stratford?
B: Contact centre. Broadband and mobile. I'm a team leader, eleven advisers, mostly retentions. And you?
A: I'm on reception at a dental practice, two days a week, and I'm doing my final year at Queen Mary, business management.
B: Final year. So the dissertation is, er, presumably going well?
A: Ha, okay, so, everyone asks that. It's going. Let's say it's going. It's on, like, consumer behaviour in skincare marketing.
B: That's quite a specific topic. Is that where you want to work, then? Brands?
A: Yeah, kind of, marketing or brand partnerships, maybe beauty or fashion. I'm gonna look at grad schemes after I hand in. My parents are like, why aren't you applying now, but, you know.
B: I'm afraid I'm probably on your parents' side there. My son is doing A-levels and I say the same thing every evening. He doesn't like it either.
A: No, totally, I get it. My dad's a pharmacist and my mum's an accountant, so I think they kind of assumed I'd do one of those. Business was, like, the compromise.
B: My wife works in a pharmacy, actually. Dispensing. She'd tell you it's a respectable life and a very repetitive one.
A: That's exactly what my dad says when he's had a long day! So what do you do outside work, are you into anything?
B: Galleries, mostly. I go on my own, on a weekday off. Tate Modern, the Barbican. There's an exhibition coming at the Barbican I've been, er, sort of counting down to.
A: Oh, that's nice. I've been to a couple of the immersive ones, like the light ones where you lie on beanbags. Mostly for the pictures, I'm not gonna lie.
B: Honest, at least. I'll admit I'm not their target audience. I prefer the kind where nobody is lying on anything. And you? Weekends?
A: Brunch. Walthamstow, mostly, or Hackney. Too much brunch, honestly. And trashy TV with my boyfriend.
B: Walthamstow. There's a Turkish place there near the market I rate very highly. The lamb is excellent. If you ever get bored of brunch.
A: Ooh, okay, send me the name. Well, you can't, but, you know. I'll find it.
B: It's on Hoe Street. You'll find it. I think that's our time.
A: Oh, yeah. Nice to meet you, Tariq. Good luck with the Barbican thing.
B: Thank you. And with the dissertation. Apply before you hand in.
A: Ha, okay, okay. Bye!
